step1_analysis.description: A differential source follower circuit acting as a voltage buffer. It provides high input impedance and low output impedance to drive subsequent stages (like filters) without loading the preceding stage, typically with a voltage gain slightly less than unity.

paper_reference.title: A Fully Integrated TV Tuner Front-End with 3.1dB NF, >+31dBm OIP3, >83dB HRR3/5 and >68dB HRR7

voltage_gain.description: Differential AC voltage gain of the buffer.

paper_reported.value: System gain not explicitly isolated for this block

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain = gm / (gm + gmb + gds). With Id ~ 100uA, gm ~ 0.75mS. Gain is typically 0.8 to 0.9 V/V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Source followers have a voltage gain slightly less than 0 dB due to the body effect and finite output resistance of the current sink.

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the output impedance (1/gm) and load capacitance. Without explicit load, parasitic capacitance dominates.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Source followers typically have very high bandwidth, easily exceeding the 870MHz operating frequency mentioned in the paper.

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumption of the buffer.

sky130_expected.calculation: VDD * (Id1 + Id4). With VBIAS=0.7V, Id ~ 100uA per branch. Total current ~ 200uA. Power = 1.8V * 200uA = 360uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends heavily on the bias voltage applied to the current sinks (N4, N5).

sky130_expected.calculation: Buffer linearity is typically high due to local negative feedback of the source follower.
sky130_expected.reasoning: While the system achieves >+31dBm, the buffer itself must have high linearity to not degrade the overall OIP3.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, AC voltage gain, -3dB bandwidth, and transient peak-to-peak gain of the differential source follower.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Differential Source Follower Testbench
.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u

XM1 VOUTP N4 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 VDD N0 VOUTN GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 VDD N6 VOUTP GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 VOUTN N5 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
* Bias for current sinks
VB1 N4 0 0.7
VB2 N5 0 0.7

* Differential inputs (N6=VINP, N0=VINN)
VCM VCM 0 1.2
VINP N6 VCM DC 0 AC 0.5 SIN(0 0.1 10MEG 0 0)
VINN N0 VCM DC 0 AC -0.5 SIN(0 -0.1 10MEG 0 0)

* Dependent sources to calculate differential signals
E_OUT VOUT_DIFF 0 VOUTP VOUTN 1.0
E_IN VIN_DIFF 0 N6 N0 1.0

.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.control
* DC Operating Point
op
let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
print power
print v(VOUTP) v(VOUTN)

* AC Analysis for Gain and Bandwidth
ac dec 20 1MEG 10G
* Since VIN_DIFF AC magnitude is 1.0, vdb(VOUT_DIFF) is the gain in dB
let gain_db = vdb(VOUT_DIFF)
meas ac midband_gain_db find gain_db at=10MEG
let gain_db_3db = midband_gain_db - 3
meas ac bw_3db when gain_db = gain_db_3db fall=1

* Transient Analysis for large-signal swing
tran 1n 500n
meas tran vout_diff_pp pp v(VOUT_DIFF)
* Input differential peak-to-peak is 0.4V (0.2V amplitude)
let gain_tran = vout_diff_pp / 0.4
print gain_tran

quit
.endc
